decisive_items: Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³ (57% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 81 mg/dL, and glucose 57 mg/dL (serum 121 mg/dL)
Repeat lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 30 cm H₂O, 1762 WBCs/mm³ (60% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 123 mg/dL, glucose 30 mg/dL (serum 105 mg/dL), and no red cells.
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement.
response.rationale: Pyogenic brain abscess best fits IV drug use, febrile leukocytosis, focal deficit, basal ganglia cerebritis evolving to a necrotic ring-enhancing mass, and neutrophilic hypoglycorrhachic CSF. Toxoplasmosis is the closest imaging mimic but is less consistent with the PMN-predominant low-glucose CSF and was not supported by protozoal investigations.

rejected.why: Transthoracic echocardiography showed no valvular vegetations, making endocarditis unlikely despite fever and leukocytosis.
CSF pleocytosis with low glucose and later ring enhancement are atypical for PML, and JC virus PCR was negative.
Rickettsial studies were negative, and the CSF/imaging pattern is more consistent with a focal pyogenic process.
Cerebral vasculitis would not explain the progressive necrotic ring-enhancing abscess evolution or the marked neutrophilic hypoglycorrhachic CSF.
